paths.description: Homepage listing and global chrome; represents primary discovery, consent, age verification, preferences, mobile reflow, performance, privacy, and accessibility.
Representative video-detail/watch journey; covers media presentation, entitlement interruption, overlays, CLS, and raw-HTML discoverability.
Distinct category/index template; covers catalog navigation, content hierarchy, and mobile reflow.
Membership selection template; covers pricing, commitments, commercial clarity, and responsive layout.
Hash-routed sign-in modal and blank-submission interaction; covers authentication, autofill, labels, validation, and recovery.
Representative unknown route; covers HTTP/runtime failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The site imposes one dark theme instead of following the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The preferences probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no prefers-color-scheme/color-scheme CSS; the dark-emulation screenshot is visually identical to the default screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining the current dark palette as one option.

findings.summary: Motion is not adapted for users who request reduced motion.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no prefers-reduced-motion rule, while the UI CSS contains 100–200ms transitions and fade/transform animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes non-essential transforms, fades, and auto-advance while preserving state feedback.

findings.summary: Route and modal state changes use abrupt custom swaps without View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered stylesheet inspection found no view-transition usage; the sign-in and detail states appear as custom overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for modal/state changes and cross-document transitions for compatible route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide static navigation chrome without scroll-state or progress feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage content is over 21,000 CSS pixels tall, while rendered CSS contains no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact sticky header that responds to scroll direction/state and an unobtrusive progress or back-to-top affordance on long listings.

findings.summary: Stacked consent, age-verification, and subscription layers obscure primary content on entry.
findings.evidence: The detail screenshot shows a subscription modal over dimmed video content, a cookie modal over that modal, and an age-verification bar above both.
findings.suggestedFix: Sequence mandatory notices instead of stacking them, defer subscription promotion until intent is shown, and guarantee an immediate, obvious dismiss path.

findings.summary: Modal and transient UI are implemented as custom containers instead of semantic dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM reports zero dialog, popover, and details elements despite visible sign-in, consent, and subscription overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal flows and popover for transient menus, including native focus management, Escape handling, and light dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Core content routes render a 769px layout into a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout captures for home, categories, and video detail each report scrollWidth/innerWidth 769 against a 360px visual viewport, producing 409px horizontal overflow. Join is the only tested template without overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the desktop minimum width, size grids and navigation intrinsically, and test all content templates at 320–400px widths.

findings.summary: Reusable content components rely on global layout rules and do not adapt to their containers.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no @container rules, and three content templates retain a 769px layout at a 360px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/navigation components containment and use container queries plus intrinsic sizing so they adapt where embedded.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus disappears on important controls and many touch targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline:none on Start verification, search, notifications, cart, Sign in, Join now, and other controls. Lighthouse found 137 target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and provide at least 24×24 CSS-pixel targets with adequate spacing, preferably 44×44 for primary mobile controls.

findings.summary: The representative watch flow is interrupted before the user can evaluate or play the selected content.
findings.evidence: Opening a video detail automatically shows the membership chooser, with the cookie prompt layered above it and age verification still present.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users reach a stable detail/player state first; present age gating once, consent once, and membership requirements at the moment playback entitlement is needed.

findings.summary: Blank sign-in submission produces no visible or programmatic validation state.
findings.evidence: After dismissing cookies and activating Sign in with empty fields, the probe found no :invalid elements, aria-invalid state, alert, or live-region message.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required fields, validate after attempted submission, move focus to the first invalid field, and announce concise recovery guidance in a live region.

findings.summary: Load performance is slow and key templates shift substantially.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.0s, TBT 360ms, and Speed Index 6.2s. The trace measured FCP/LCP 4.37s. Detail and join mobile layouts observed CLS 0.239 and 0.221.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reserve overlay/media space, defer non-critical work, and establish per-template LCP/CLS budgets.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers about 5 MB across 188 requests, with avoidable image and render-blocking cost.
findings.evidence: HAR summary reports 4,980,826 transferred bytes, including 3,152,223 image bytes and 1,476,567 script bytes; Lighthouse estimates 778 KiB image savings and 1,370ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize only the true LCP image, lazy-load below-fold media, right-size/modernize thumbnails, and shorten critical CSS/resource chains.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped CSS and JavaScript are unused on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 773 KiB unused JavaScript and 98 KiB unused CSS; Google Tag Manager alone transfers about 304 KiB across two scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route/feature, remove duplicate analytics bootstraps, and load consented third-party code only when needed.

findings.summary: Many controls and links lack accessible names, and form controls lack labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 3 unnamed buttons, 132 unnamed links, and an unlabeled VR checkbox; DOM inspection found no main landmark and hundreds of unnamed visible controls/links.
findings.suggestedFix: Name icon-only controls, label all inputs, remove empty focusable links, use native button semantics, and add a main landmark.

findings.summary: Age-verification and promotional text fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven contrast failures, including white/green age-verification text at 2.42:1 and discount badges at 4.04:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the green and red surfaces or adjust foreground colors so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large text reaches 3:1.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark, and focus structure is not reliable for keyboard and assistive-technology users.
findings.evidence: The page has two H1 elements, skips to H4 for age verification/footer headings, has no main/nav/header/footer landmarks in the rendered probe, and removes focus outlines on primary controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page H1, a logical heading hierarchy and semantic landmarks; preserve visible focus for every interactive element and trap/restore focus in dialogs.

findings.summary: The production viewport disables zoom and core templates fail narrow-screen reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured user-scalable=0 with maximum-scale=1.0, 137 undersized targets, and the layout primitive measured 409px overflow at 360px on three core templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable/max-scale restrictions, fix intrinsic reflow, and enlarge/space touch targets.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery are inconsistent despite a valid document shell.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 8 images without dimensions, 32 oversized images, 40 below-fold images without lazy loading, and 73 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every image, generate correctly sized modern-format variants, and lazy-load non-critical media.

findings.summary: Browser platform diagnostics show avoidable lifecycle and cookie issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports BFCache blocked by Cache-Control: no-store after cookie modification and Cookie issues in DevTools; the best-practices score is 0.77.
findings.suggestedFix: Review no-store usage so safe pages can use BFCache and resolve browser cookie diagnostics without weakening account privacy.

findings.summary: Some navigation controls are uncrawlable and the mobile viewport policy is hostile to users.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) anchors and a failing crawlable-anchors audit; the viewport disables scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real hrefs for destinations, and a scalable mobile viewport.

findings.summary: Canonical and robots signals are present, but the conventional sitemap endpoint returns 404.
findings.evidence: The probe found a correct canonical and crawlable robots.txt, while /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index at /sitemap.xml (or advertise its actual location in robots.txt) and keep it aligned with canonical public routes.

findings.summary: Rich video pages do not expose structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: Rendered probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph properties, despite video detail and catalog entities that qualify for VideoObject/Breadcrumb metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject, BreadcrumbList, and organization JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but cookie and CSP settings leave avoidable exposure.
findings.evidence: Nine of 13 cookies lack Secure; several use SameSite=None. CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. X-Content-Type-Options is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use the strictest workable SameSite setting, remove CSP unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline via nonces or hashes, and send nosniff.

findings.summary: A sensitive-content page makes a large third-party and analytics footprint before consent is resolved.
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR capture recorded 11 third-party origins, 185 third-party requests, 4.88 MB third-party transfer, and Google Tag Manager. Google analytics cookies are set for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics until consent, minimize identifiers and retention, consolidate requests, and self-host or remove third parties that do not add user value.

findings.summary: Authentication offers passwords and federated identity but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The sign-in state exposes email/password, xHamster, and Google choices; rendered code inspection found no WebAuthn/passkey surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and sign-in alongside existing recovery/federation, and retain contextual permission requests only.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete or overbroad.
findings.evidence: Referrer-Policy is absent; Permissions-Policy grants camera, fullscreen, accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer to all origins; CSP is broadly permissive though HSTS and frame protections are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict Referrer-Policy, allow sensitive capabilities only for required origins/features, tighten CSP, and add nosniff.

findings.summary: Independent overlay systems collide instead of producing one robust top-layer state.
findings.evidence: The video detail screenshot shows subscription and cookie modals simultaneously, with the age banner also active; the DOM uses no native top-layer primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Centralize overlay state, use dialog/popover top-layer primitives, and prevent a second modal from opening while another blocking decision is unresolved.

findings.summary: Language is declared, but layout CSS is not prepared for bidirectional or alternate writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang="en" is present, but dir is absent and rendered CSS inspection found no logical margin/padding/inset/size properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction explicitly or derive it by locale and migrate physical left/right layout rules to logical properties.

findings.summary: Sign-in errors are not prevented or announced humanely.
findings.evidence: Blank submission yielded no required validity state, aria-invalid attribute, alert, or live-region message.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction/submission, preserve entered values, and announce errors with field-specific recovery text.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields do not use the standard autocomplete tokens needed by password managers.
findings.evidence: Username/email uses autocomplete="email" rather than username, and password inputs expose no autocomplete token.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and autocomplete="current-password"; preserve password-manager and paste behavior.

findings.summary: Image assets are substantially oversized and frequently delivered in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 32 oversized images, 73 legacy-format images, and 40 below-fold images without lazy loading; Lighthouse estimates 778 KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, right-size avatars/thumbnails, and lazy-load below-fold images.

findings.summary: Third-party and media transfer is disproportionate before the user chooses or plays content.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 4.88 MB and 185 requests from third-party origins; 151 images transfer 3.15 MB and scripts transfer 1.48 MB on the initial listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a consent-aware third-party budget, defer media to viewport/intent, and cap initial listing depth and bytes.

taskList.title: Fix responsive reflow, zoom, focus, and target sizing
Stop stacking entry overlays and use semantic top-layer primitives
Fix names, labels, landmarks, heading order, and contrast
Cut initial media/script cost and stabilize templates
Harden cookies, CSP, permissions, and third-party collection
Add humane sign-in validation and autofill tokens
Restore crawlable navigation, sitemap, and entity metadata
Improve navigation state and transition continuity
